I am currently working as a Case Manager at Broward Partnership for the Homeless, where I began my journey in human services in July 2025. This experience has been incredibly valuable and has allowed me to grow both professionally and personally while developing a deeper understanding of the needs of the individuals and families I serve.
When I began this position, I anticipated maintaining a caseload of approximately 30 clients, which I understood would allow me to provide each individual with the attention, advocacy, and support they deserve. However, my caseload has grown to approximately 50 clients. While I remain committed to serving my clients effectively, the increased workload has made it challenging to provide the level of individualized service I believe is essential to being an effective case manager.
I initially intended to supplement my income by working a second job, but the demands of my current caseload make that unrealistic. My current salary is approximately $45,000 annually, and I am seeking an opportunity that provides greater financial stability while allowing me to remain fully committed to a career in human services.
I am passionate about helping others and want to continue building my career in this field. I am looking for an organization where I can bring my experience, compassion, and dedication to the work while earning a salary that provides the financial stability necessary for me to focus fully on my professional responsibilities. My goal is to find a position where I can be fully engaged, give 100% to the individuals I serve, and continue growing as a human services professional.

questionnaire.response:
In my previous position, I served as a Residential Program Director with Sunrise Community, where I was responsible for overseeing two group homes and supervising a team of approximately 20 staff members. My salary was $45,000 yearly but was raised to $55,000 after 3 months. This role was highly rewarding and provided me with valuable experience supporting individuals with mental health and intellectual disabilities. I found the work especially meaningful because it allowed me to advocate for the individuals we served while ensuring they received appropriate care, support, and services.

During my tenure (July 2024-2025), one of the homes under my supervision was closed, and I was subsequently transferred to Miami to manage two additional residential homes. This transition presented several significant operational challenges, including the need to work directly on the staff floor while simultaneously fulfilling my managerial responsibilities. In addition, there were ongoing operational and compliance concerns within the homes that created potential liabilities.

I made every effort to address these concerns through the appropriate management channels and advocated for the necessary corrective actions. Unfortunately, when several of the issues remained unresolved despite my efforts to bring them to upper management's attention, I ultimately made the difficult decision to leave the organization.

Despite the circumstances surrounding my departure, I remain grateful for the experience and the opportunity to serve individuals with disabilities. The position strengthened my leadership, problem-solving, staff-management, advocacy, and crisis-management skills, all of which continue to shape my approach to working in human services.

candidates.cover_letter:
Dear Hiring Manager,

I am excited to apply for the Outreach Manager – Behavioral Health position. With extensive experience in community outreach, healthcare support, relationship building, program coordination, and administrative leadership, I bring a strong ability to connect individuals and families with essential services while developing meaningful partnerships throughout the community.

In my experience as an Outreach Specialist with Compass Health Network, I worked directly with individuals and families to help them access Medicaid, SNAP, health insurance marketplace coverage, behavioral health resources, and other community-based services. I collaborated with case managers, healthcare providers, and community organizations to coordinate services, strengthen referral relationships, and help ensure individuals received the support they needed.

My background has also given me experience conducting follow-up outreach, educating communities about available programs, maintaining accurate documentation, tracking outcomes, preparing reports, and identifying community needs and trends. I understand that successful behavioral health outreach requires more than promoting services—it requires trust, compassion, consistency, and strong relationships with both community partners and the people being served.

In an Outreach Manager role, I would bring a proactive and organized leadership style focused on expanding community partnerships, strengthening referral networks, increasing awareness of behavioral health services, and supporting measurable outreach goals. My 20 years of administrative experience have further strengthened my ability to manage competing priorities, communicate professionally, maintain confidentiality, and follow through on important details.

I would welcome the opportunity to bring my outreach experience, relationship-building skills, and commitment to helping people access meaningful resources to your organization. Thank you for considering my application. I look forward to the opportunity to discuss how my experience can contribute to your behavioral health outreach initiatives and continued growth.

Sincerely,

Cathy Hull
